records.name: IDV1
records.title: A/C feed ratio change with B composition constant
records.base_description: A step disturbance changes the A/C feed ratio in stream 4 while the B composition remains constant. The fault affects reactant balance, reactor feed composition, reaction rate, recycle composition, and downstream separator and stripper behavior.
records.semantic_text: The disturbance originates from a step change in the A/C feed ratio within stream 4, while maintaining constant B composition. This fault impacts several unit operations, including the reactor where reactant balance and reaction rate are altered, the recycle system due to changes in composition, and downstream separators and strippers whose behavior is affected by the modified feed ratio. The propagated variables include deviations in the A/C ratio within stream 4, shifts in downstream product qualities, and variations in composition measurements across the reactor and recycle streams. This semantic prototype is valuable for zero-shot diagnosis as it enables recognition of fault patterns through observed variable changes without prior examples, facilitating rapid troubleshooting by linking disturbance propagation to measurable effects.

records.name: IDV2
records.title: B composition change with A/C ratio constant
records.base_description: A step disturbance changes the B composition in stream 4 while the A/C ratio remains constant. The inert component changes gas-phase dilution, reactor pressure, purge flow, recycle stream composition, and product separation behavior.
records.semantic_text: A step disturbance in stream 4 alters the B composition while maintaining a constant A/C ratio, originating from an unexpected change in feedstock quality or process control malfunction. This affects several unit operations, including gas-phase dilution, reactor pressure regulation, purge flow adjustments, and product separation efficiency. The disturbance propagates through variables such as reactor pressure, which influences purge flow rates, and alters the composition of the recycle stream, impacting downstream separation units. This semantic prototype is valuable for zero-shot diagnosis because it captures how a single disturbance can propagate across interconnected process variables, enabling identification of root causes without prior fault examples by leveraging mechanistic understanding of variable interactions.

records.name: IDV4
records.title: Reactor cooling water inlet temperature step
records.base_description: A step disturbance changes reactor cooling water inlet temperature. The fault directly perturbs reactor heat removal, reactor temperature, cooling water outlet temperature, reaction rate, pressure, recycle composition, and downstream separator conditions.
records.semantic_text: The IDV4 fault originates from an unexpected step disturbance in the reactor cooling water inlet temperature, likely caused by external factors such as utility supply fluctuations or control system malfunctions. This perturbation directly impacts the reactor's heat removal efficiency, leading to changes in reactor temperature, outlet temperature, and reaction rate. Consequently, pressure variations occur within the reactor, affecting the recycle composition and downstream separator operations. The propagated variables include deviations in cooling water flow, pressure adjustments in the separator, and potential shifts in product quality. This semantic prototype is valuable for zero-shot diagnosis as it enables the identification of root causes by linking observed anomalies across interconnected units to a single disturbance source, even without prior fault examples.
